title: How can one Binairo row be filled with no guessing?
description: A Binairo row of six cells has horizontal lines in the first two cells and a vertical line in the fifth. The two rules, equal numbers of each line and never three alike side by side, fill the other cells one at a time. Keeko doubts the fourth cell.
teaching_notes: One idea: fill the cell next to a pair first, then use the count of each kind to finish the row. Watch for students who copy the neighbour's line and make three alike in a row.

source: In a Binairo row of 6 cells, the first two cells hold horizo
video_script.why: The child applies the two Binairo rules in order to fill one row without guessing.
video_script.substitution: Fill the cell next to a pair first, check the other neighbour, then count each kind to finish the row.
video_script.anchor: a Binairo puzzle card showing one row of six cells, with horizontal lines in cells one and two and a vertical line in cell five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko makes cell four vertical to match cell five. Then cells three, four and five are all vertical, three alike side by side, which the second rule forbids.
video_script.payoff_line: the row is horizontal, horizontal, vertical, horizontal, vertical, vertical

final_answer.value: H H V H V V
final_answer.spoken: horizontal, horizontal, vertical, horizontal, vertical, vertical

hold_back: H H V H V V
never_show: cell 4 filled with V marked as right
maths_rules: rule one: a row of 6 cells has 3 horizontal and 3 vertical lines
rule two: no three alike side by side
cells 1 and 2 are H, so cell 3 must be V
cells 3 and 5 are V; if cell 4 were V then cells 3, 4, 5 are V V V, so cell 4 is H
H is now in cells 1, 2, 4 which makes 3, so cell 6 must be V
check: 3 H and 3 V; longest run of alike is 2
video_script.design: One idea: use the pair first, then the count. Wrong idea: copy the neighbour. The puzzle card stays in the anchor band and the working goes on the board.
open_questions: The row in the worklist is a worked example and is not printed in the book text, which gives only the rules and puzzle grids.
